question: Maria and James are comparing their project budgets. Maria starts with 130 dollars. She divides by 5 for her weekly allocation. She spends 6 dollars. She multiplies by 3 for monthly planning. She adds 68 dollars in additional funding. She multiplies by 6 for annual projections. She adds 10 dollars in interest. James has budgeted 200 dollars for his project. What is Maria's annual budget projection?

A farm starts with 123 bushels of grain. They add 20 bushels from harvesting. They multiply by 6 to distribute to 6 locations. They subtract 683 bushels for animal feed. They multiply by 3 to plan for 3 seasons. They add 77 bushels from a donation. The farm has 45 workers. Converting to metric tons, what is their final grain amount?

A production facility starts with 67 units. They multiply by 7 for a weekly forecast. They add 55 units from a new line. They multiply by 6 to plan across 6 shifts. They add 37 units from inventory recovery. They subtract 550 units for shipping. Converting to dozens, what is the final unit count?

Rachel and David track their fitness progress throughout the day. Rachel starts with 92 steps taken. In the morning, she adds 11 more steps. By afternoon, she loses 21 steps (removing miscount). She doubles her step count by 2 for walking routes. By evening, she loses 114 steps to app errors. David walked 80 steps today. How many steps did Rachel actually achieve?

A warehouse manages its inventory throughout the shift. It starts with 174 items. It adds 35 items from the morning delivery. It loses 107 items to shipment. It gains 60 items from returns. It adds 3 more items from a correction. How many items remain in the warehouse?

A storage unit starts with 117 containers. They multiply by 5 to account for 5 warehouse locations. They multiply by 6 to prepare for 6 months of supply. They add 62 containers from overflow. They subtract 1194 containers for large orders. How many containers remain in their total inventory?

A daycare center operates through three shifts. They start with 105 children in their database. In the morning, they add 24 more children. By afternoon, they add 64 additional children. They multiply by 6 to calculate staff needed (6 children per staff). They multiply by 5 to plan for 5 days of the week. Converting to dozens of children, how many staff are needed?

A manufacturing plant starts with 187 products. They add 80 products from production. They subtract 26 products with defects. They multiply by 8 for shipment to 8 stores. They multiply by 4 to account for 4 shipments per month. They divide by 2 to distribute evenly between 2 regions. They multiply by 9 for a 9-month inventory plan. Converting to thousands, what is the annual product count?

A store manager tracks daily inventory through all shifts. They start with 162 items. In the morning, they add 50 items from delivery. They divide by 2 to organize into 2 sections. By afternoon, they lose 61 items to sales. By evening, they add 80 more items. They multiply by 4 to forecast the next 4 days. Converting to dozens, what is the forecasted inventory?

A production line operates through the day. They start with 118 units. They multiply by 6 for 6 hours of production. They divide by 2 to split between morning and afternoon output. They multiply by 6 for 6 product variants. They multiply by 5 for 5-unit batches. They add 69 units from overflow. How many units are produced today?

A shop starts with 22 items in stock. In the morning, they lose 21 items to sales. By afternoon, they receive 58 items from delivery. By mid-afternoon, they add 10 more items. By evening, they add 72 more items. How many items are in stock at day's end?

A business operates through the day. They start with 229 dollars. In the morning, they lose 126 dollars to operating costs. By mid-day, they multiply by 7 in revenue. By afternoon, they add 44 dollars. They multiply by 6 for a multi-branch calculation. They lose 2382 dollars in taxes. The business opened a dozen years ago. What is their final balance?

A farm starts with 43 items. They multiply by 9 to scale up production. They multiply by 3 for 3 growing seasons. They add 12 items from new equipment. They lose 1085 items to market distribution. They add 27 items from equipment. The farm operates 15 fields. Converting to tons, what is their final production?

A manufacturer starts with 184 units. They add 63 units from new production. They multiply by 7 to account for 7 assembly lines. They subtract 1235 units for a major order. They lose 100 units to scrap. They lose 174 more units to quality checks. Converting to dozens, how many units pass quality?

A factory starts production with 98 items. They lose 50 items due to quality issues. They multiply by 9 for a scaled-up month. They multiply by 4 for quarterly planning. They multiply by 4 for annual planning. What is the annual production forecast?

A store tracks inventory throughout the day. They start with 73 items. They add 69 items from a new shipment. They lose 126 items to sales. They add 48 items from returns. They lose 21 items to damage. They double the remaining count by 2 for planning. The store manager has worked 15 years. Converting to dozens, how many items does the store have?

A bakery starts with 48 cups of flour. They lose 32 cups for large orders. They lose 13 more cups to waste. They multiply by 7 to scale for a week. They multiply by 9 for a month's supply. They add 45 cups from new stock. They add 54 more cups from delivery. Converting to gallons, what is their total flour?

A daycare starts with 197 children on enrollment. In the morning, they lose 18 to cancellations. By afternoon, they add 28 from new registrations. By evening, they lose 60 to departures. They multiply by 4 to forecast capacity needs. They multiply by 3 for a three-season plan. What is their total capacity planning number?

A farm operates throughout the day. They start with 86 bushels of grain. In the morning, they add 24 bushels from harvest. By afternoon, they add 76 more bushels. They multiply by 5 for five storage facilities. They multiply by 3 for three seasonal rotations. The farm has 40 workers. Converting to tons, what is their total grain?

A warehouse starts with 214 units. They add 8 units from a late delivery. They lose 22 units to damage. They add 20 units from returns. They multiply by 9 to account for 9 distribution centers. They multiply by 4 for quadruple scaling. They multiply by 8 to project across 8 months. Converting to thousands, what is the total?

A warehouse operates throughout the day. They start with 164 packages. In the morning, they add 47 packages. By mid-day, they add 60 more. By afternoon, they lose 230 to shipment. By late afternoon, they add 65 from returns. They divide by 2 to prepare two shipments. The facility opened a dozen years ago. How many packages per shipment?

A business starts with 142 items in inventory. They add 63 items from production. They add 40 items from suppliers. They multiply by 7 to forecast for 7 weeks. They add 40 more items from recovery. They multiply by 9 to project quarterly. Converting to units, what is their quarterly projection?

A warehouse starts with 40 units. They multiply by 6 for six warehouse locations. They add 6 units from overflow. They multiply by 2 for a double-shift plan. They add 4 units from correction. They multiply by 7 for a seven-day forecast. They multiply by 8 for an eight-week plan. The manager has 22 years experience. What is their eight-week projection?

Alex and Maria compare their savings accounts. Alex starts with 108 dollars. He loses 105 dollars to expenses. He doubles his remaining amount by 2. He loses 5 more dollars to a fee. He multiplies by 7 for a seven-month projection. Maria has saved 200 dollars. What is Alex's seven-month projection?

A production facility starts with 214 items. They multiply by 5 to scale production. They lose 387 items to quality control. They lose 321 more items to defects. They multiply by 5 to forecast for 5 shifts. They add 32 units from recovery. Converting to dozens, what is the final count?
